docker_execution.what_ran: A disposable container from the official Python image pinned by digest, with the core restrictions core/execution.py applies (no network, read-only root, all capabilities dropped, no-new-privileges, user 1000:1000, memory and pid limits). Not applied here: its --cpus, --ipc/--cgroupns private, tmpfs mounts, log driver, and exact pid/memory values.
docker_execution.command: docker run --rm --network none --read-only --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --user 1000:1000 --memory 256m --pids-limit 64 python@sha256:82bc3c539b8813ada9d68c63b40158fa002f7f33de9bf3312a3dfdc0620dff56 python -I -c <probe: print version and arch, try a TCP connect to 1.1.1.1:80, try to write /x>

web_search.what_ran: agent/web_search.py (web_search_tool + SearxngBackend) against a local searxng/searxng container, called directly from Python 3.14.4 in WSL2 at commit 70e5215.
web_search.backend_endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8888 (bound to loopback only; settings enable the json format and disable the limiter; the generated secret_key stays outside the repository)

1. What's new in Python 3.14 — Python 3.14.7 documentation

measurement_limits: The Docker run did not go through core/execution.py (DockerExecutionBackend). That path needs a runtime receipt from ci/prepare_runtime.py, which needs an owner-reviewed external trust file; that step is the owner's (ci/README.md) and was not performed. So this proves Docker runs an isolated container on this host, not that Diwan's execution backend does.
The isolation checks are two probes (one outbound TCP connect, one root write); they are not a sandbox-escape audit.
web_search was called directly, not by a model inside the agent loop; no live model chose the tool.
Two queries, one SearXNG instance with default engines; result quality and engine availability vary by time and region.
No result contained instruction-like text, so quarantine was exercised only on clean input (quarantined is empty); its behavior on hostile snippets is covered by tests, not by this run.
Python 3.14.4 was the WSL system interpreter, not the project uv environment: uv sync fails on this host because editdistance (via camel-tools) has no cp314 wheel and no C compiler is installed.
ج٥ depends on ع٣ (the diwan-live runner), which is not done.
